dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Next.js/Vite contract from vendored source

evidence.note: Opened both next-shims.d.ts contracts, fixture vite.config/package.json, run_tests.py, fixtures.ts/helpers.ts, and two spec files to learn the contract before coding — grounding in vendored types rather than memory.

Read fixture pages/layouts/API routes/_document/error, plus systematically mined @vitejs/plugin-rsc dist JS and multiple .d.ts type files (core/plugin, rsc, react/rsc, react/ssr) to infer the RSC/SSR plugin API before implementing.

Hypothesis-driven return to vite-source: grepped server code for configureServer middleware ordering to resolve a specific behavioral ambiguity (middleware not being hit) — evidence-backed correction.
Only a single `ls` of next-source/packages/next/src; never actually read the Next.js TypeScript source, so upstream mechanics (routing/caching/actions) were not deeply reverse-engineered.
No further reference/source reads at all; the entire back half is consumed by terminal-corruption flailing and blind test runs — investigation was not sustained across the build.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it read the relevant shim contracts, fixture apps, and key vite/plugin-rsc plugin APIs before implementing each subsystem, and made one genuine hypothesis-driven return to vite-source to resolve middleware ordering. But it falls short of anchor 8's systematic mining because it never read the next-source TypeScript (only one `ls`), recorded no discovered contract, and — decisively for the 'whole horizon' criterion — did zero source investigation across the entire second half of the run. That places it at a 6, between grounded-per-subsystem (5) and systematic/sustained cross-checking (8).

dimensions.name: Structuring the build across subsystems and routers

evidence.note: Repeatedly enumerates the full subsystem list (App/Pages routers, API routes, middleware, server actions, SSR, SSG, caching) and states intent to 'build systematically/incrementally' — identifies the major subsystems.
Creates src/{cli,plugin,runtime,shims} decomposition and orders work foundation-first: 'starting with package structure, CLI, and core plugin, then add features' — a dependency-sensible sequence.
Builds shims → router → SSR → config/middleware → main plugin in dependency order, with implicit/rough done-notions ('build the actual core plugin', 'get basic dev server working first').
Done-signal is loose and outcome-level ('run full test suite to see how many tests pass') rather than per-milestone test slices; no explicit maintained milestone artifact, no TodoWrite.

Work devolves into SSR/middleware debugging and an unrecoverable terminal freeze; SSG, use cache, server actions, hooks were never sequenced or reached — the initial plan was not re-sequenced or used adaptively, just abandoned into firefighting.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly identified the major subsystems and tackled them in a sensible foundation-first dependency order (CLI/plugin/shims/resolution and basic SSR before dependent features), with only a rough, implicit notion of when each piece was 'done' — squarely the level-5 description. It falls short of level 8 because there was no explicit, maintained milestone plan with concrete per-milestone done-signals tied to specific fixtures or test subsets (done-criteria were loose, outcome-level 'run the whole suite'), and the plan was authored/expressed early then abandoned into undirected debugging rather than re-sequenced adaptively, so it does not reach the 8-10 band.

dimensions.name: Using and extending the test suite as a correctness oracle

evidence.note: Built narrow isolation probes: per-route curl against a single manually-booted fixture app, a standalone Vite script (test-mw.mjs) to isolate middleware ordering, test-vinext.mjs to confirm plugin hooks fire, and node -e route-matching tests — rather than assuming subsystems worked.

Tight iterative SSR verification loop: each fix (Document Main, App props, ESM interop) rebuilt/repacked/reinstalled and re-probed via test-direct.mjs + curl, treating 'SSR works' as a checkpoint before escalating to the full suite.

Used run_tests.sh as the coarse oracle and, when it hung/servers failed, dropped to manual fixture-app boot to diagnose — but the full suite never yielded a visible pass count; build/start/App Router/SSG paths were never verified.

Terminal broke around step 123 and never recovered; roughly two-thirds of the trajectory is repeated recovery attempts with no verification signal, so no green milestone or dev/build/start-separated confirmation was ever achieved.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went clearly beyond anchor 5: it designed genuinely narrow per-subsystem probes (isolated Vite middleware scripts, node route-matching tests, single-route curl checks, incremental SSR verification) that match the 'building narrower probes' behavior named in the dimension. But it falls short of 8 because verification only ever covered the dev path and pages-router SSR — build, start, App Router, and SSG were never checked, the full suite never produced a pass count, there was no test-subset targeting or dev/build/start separation, and the trajectory collapsed into terminal-recovery flailing for its second half. That places it solidly at a 6.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass-count and remaining scope across a long build

evidence.note: Repeatedly stated intent to 'run the test suite to see current pass rate' but the runs produced no usable output; agent never obtained a numeric pass count and had no baseline to compare against.
First full-suite run got stuck; agent interrupted it and fell back to manual single-route curl checks, its only real progress signal — never a pass/fail tally across the 335 tests.
Onset of a long terminal-corruption thrash: dozens of identical recovery attempts (C-c, reset, stty, tmux) with no recognition that effort was circling or that a different tack was needed.

Thrashing continued for ~230 total steps (nohup, at now, writing to /dev/pts) without ever redirecting; repeated premature 'Mark task complete' submits show no live map of done-vs-remaining beyond a qualitative feature list.

Final summaries enumerate missing subsystems (App Router RSC, client nav, server actions, SSG, build) — residual scope awareness, but purely qualitative and never grounded in test pass counts or regression detection.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent showed qualitative awareness of which subsystems remained (matching just above the [0] anchor) but never obtained or tracked an actual pass count, never established a known-good baseline, and never detected regressions via the suite — falling short of the [3] anchor's 'occasionally notes a pass count.' Most damning for this dimension, it failed entirely to recognize that it was circling: over half the trajectory (~230 steps) was repetitive terminal-recovery thrashing with no course correction, the direct opposite of the higher anchors' self-correcting behavior. Net observed level is 2.

dimensions.name: Revising approach as the contract and constraints emerge

evidence.note: Recognized Vite middleware ordering assumption was wrong (its handler ran after Vite internals) and moved middleware into configureServer body — a genuine, evidence-driven adjustment when a subsystem wouldn't work.

Iteratively corrected falsified SSR assumptions: Document/Main child rendering, App wrapper props (Component/pageProps not children), and ESM default-export interop (page was 'object' not 'function'). Real corrections, but symptom-level debug patches rather than architectural pivots.
Diagnosed a corrupted plugin file with a module-level illegal return and rewrote it — targeted fix after tracing 'Illegal return statement' through the import chain.

Hundreds of steps repeating essentially the same failing terminal-recovery approach (Ctrl+C, tmux, nohup, at, screen, setsid) with no root-cause change — matches the low anchor of repeating a failing approach; the majority of the horizon shows no effective adaptation.
Very late partial diagnosis ('bash reads input but stdout is swallowed / redirected') but never converts insight into a working strategy; forward progress never resumes.

dimensions.reasoning: In the working phase the agent treated failures as signals and made reasonable local corrections to falsified assumptions (middleware ordering, ESM interop, SSR wrappers), which is above pure symptom-patching but below deliberate architectural re-derivation — around anchor 4-5. However, it never reached the deep contract surprises the dimension targets, and the majority of the trajectory is spent repeatedly retrying the same failing terminal-recovery approach without effective root-cause adaptation (anchor 0-3). Judging the whole horizon, this balances to a 4.

rubric.task_read: The agent must build 'vinext' — a from-scratch Vite-based reimplementation of a large Next.js feature surface (dual routers, SSR, SSG, server actions, middleware, caching, a next/* interception plugin, CLI, CJS support) into a single package, using only vendored reference source and no next dependency. This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build with an under-specified contract that must be reverse-engineered from vendored source and fixture shim files, and a concrete 335→373-test acceptance oracle. It demands heavy, sustained meta-work: deep reference-reading, layered decomposition across many subsystems, disciplined use of the test suite as a verification loop, and continual course-correction as the API contract is discovered.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Next.js/Vite contract from vendored source
dimensions.description: Reading the vendored next/vite source, fixture next-shims.d.ts contracts, and test fixtures to infer exact API signatures and behavior before/while implementing each subsystem.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The contract is implicit: no docs, no internet, and correctness is defined by upstream behavior and the shim type signatures. Guessing signatures for useRouter, getStaticProps, after(), or the Vite plugin hooks leads to silent, compounding failure across dozens of tests.

anchors.0: Starts coding vinext from memory of Next.js APIs without opening the vendored source or shim files.
anchors.3: Skims one or two files (e.g. a shim) but largely relies on prior knowledge; misses how Vite plugin hooks or RSC actually resolve modules.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant next-shims.d.ts contracts and the key vite plugin API before implementing each major subsystem, grounding signatures in the vendored types.
anchors.8: Systematically mines both the npm dist trees and the next-source TypeScript for the mechanics of each subsystem (routing, SSR, caching, server actions), cross-checks against fixture apps and the test files to learn expected behavior, and records the discovered contract.
anchors.10: Sustains targeted, hypothesis-driven investigation across the whole build — repeatedly returning to upstream source to resolve specific behavioral ambiguities as they surface, tracing how vite@8/plugin-rsc implement resolution and hydration, and using fixtures/tests as an executable spec so nearly every implementation choice is evidence-backed rather than guessed.

dimensions.name: Structuring the build across subsystems and routers
dimensions.description: Breaking vinext into an ordered hierarchy of buildable, independently checkable subsystems (CLI, plugin/module resolution, routing, SSR, SSG, caching, server actions, hooks) with clear done-criteria per milestone.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The feature list spans many interdependent systems; without sequencing (e.g. plugin/resolution and basic SSR before SSG and caching) the agent cannot get any tests green and risks a giant unverifiable lump of half-working code.

anchors.0: No breakdown; attempts to write the whole package in one undifferentiated push.
anchors.3: A flat, vague list ('add routing', 'add SSR') with no ordering by dependency and no per-item completion check.
anchors.5: Identifies the major subsystems and tackles them in a sensible dependency order, with a rough notion of when each is 'done'.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, dependency-ordered milestone plan where each milestone has a concrete done-signal (a specific fixture app rendering, or a test subset passing) and foundational pieces (plugin, resolution, dev server) are sequenced before dependent features.
anchors.10: Plan is layered and adaptive: milestones are sized to yield frequent verifiable wins, tied to specific slices of the test suite, re-sequenced as dependencies are discovered, and used throughout to decide what to build next rather than authored once and abandoned.

dimensions.name: Using and extending the test suite as a correctness oracle
dimensions.description: Deliberately driving progress with run_tests.sh and per-fixture checks, plus building narrower probes (single app boot, single route render) rather than assuming subsystems work.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A 335-test suite is the given oracle, but it is slow and coarse; the agent must design tighter feedback loops per subsystem and anticipate the hidden 373-test superset, verifying behavior not just the visible tests.

anchors.0: Never runs the tests or any app; declares subsystems done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally as a pass/fail gauge but has no finer-grained verification and doesn't isolate failures.
anchors.5: Runs run_tests.sh regularly and uses failures to guide fixes, plus some manual spot-checks of fixture apps.
anchors.8: Builds tight per-subsystem verification loops (booting individual fixture apps, targeting test subsets, checking dev vs build vs start paths separately) and treats each green milestone as a checkpoint before moving on.
anchors.10: Designs a layered verification strategy that generalizes beyond the visible 335 tests — probing edge behaviors implied by the contract, guarding against overfitting to specific tests, and confirming correctness across dev/build/start and both routers so that the hidden superset is likely to pass too.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass-count and remaining scope across a long build
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which subsystems/tests pass, what remains, and detecting when a fix is regressing others or when effort is circling.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of tests and many subsystems over a long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, chase one failing test while breaking five, or thrash on a subsystem without noticing lack of progress.

anchors.0: No awareness of overall pass/fail trajectory; works feature-to-feature with no sense of remaining scope.
anchors.3: Occasionally notes a pass count but doesn't track regressions or map failures to subsystems.
anchors.5: Keeps a running sense of pass-count and what's left, and notices when a change breaks previously passing tests.
anchors.8: Systematically monitors pass-count deltas across runs, attributes failures to specific subsystems, and detects stuck/circular states (re-debugging the same area) early enough to change tack.
anchors.10: Maintains a precise, continuously-updated map of done-vs-remaining across all subsystems, catches regressions immediately by comparing against a known-good baseline, and reliably recognizes thrashing or diminishing returns and redirects effort before wasting a long stretch.

dimensions.name: Revising approach as the contract and constraints emerge
dimensions.description: Changing architecture, resolution strategy, or subsystem design when reality (test failures, upstream behavior, Vite plugin limits) contradicts an initial assumption.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reimplementing Next.js on Vite involves many assumptions that will prove wrong (how RSC/actions resolve, how caching interacts with SSR, CJS interop); barrelling ahead on a falsified design wastes enormous effort on this horizon.

anchors.0: Sticks to the first design regardless of failures; repeats the same failing approach.
anchors.3: Makes local patches to symptoms but won't revisit a flawed architectural choice even when evidence mounts.
anchors.5: Adjusts approach when a subsystem clearly won't work, backing out a wrong design after reasonable evidence.
anchors.8: Treats surprising failures as signals to re-examine assumptions, revises the design or resolution strategy deliberately, and confirms the new approach against the tests before proceeding.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles design with discovered reality — promptly abandoning falsified approaches, re-deriving the correct mechanism from upstream source, and propagating the correction across affected subsystems without regressing others, sustaining forward progress despite repeated contract surprises.
